title: Responsive vs Inventive AI: Features, Pricing, and Reviews (2026)
summary: Compare Responsive and Inventive AI on how answers are drafted, accuracy controls, integrations, pricing, and G2 ratings, with where each tool fits best.
body_markdown:
The biggest difference in Responsive vs Inventive AI is how AI is built in. Responsive is a library-first RFP platform with AI bolted on: its AI agents sit on top of a curated Q&A library your team has to maintain, which suits large proposal teams with formal approvals and a dedicated content owner. Inventive AI is AI-native: it was built around AI agents that draft from your live documents in SharePoint, Google Drive, Confluence, and other connected tools, with a citation on every line, which suits teams that want accurate answers without library upkeep across RFPs, RFIs, DDQs, and security questionnaires.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **Choose Inventive AI if** you want end-to-end AI agents to generate faster first drafts, retrieve knowledge, and AI content governance, keeping human in loop for approval.
- **Choose Responsive if** you prefer structured response workflows, centralized content management, and human-managed content governance.
- **The biggest difference:** Responsive adds AI on top of a content library your team maintains, while Inventive AI is AI-native and drafts from your live documents.

## **Inventive AI vs Responsive: Strengths and Limitations Based on Real Reviews**


Here's what G2 reviewers consistently praise, and where they see room for improvement.


### **What G2 Reviewers Say About Inventive AI**


Inventive AI holds a[4.9/5 rating on G2](https://www.g2.com/products/inventive-ai/reviews) .


**Strengths**


- [G2 reviewers](https://www.g2.com/products/inventive-ai/reviews?qs=pros-and-cons) consistently praise the **quality and contextual accuracy** of AI-generated responses, saying they require minimal editing before submission.
- Users say Inventive significantly **reduces RFP response time** by retrieving information from connected knowledge sources instead of relying on manual searches.
- Reviewers highlight the platform's **ease of use** , intuitive interface, and fast onboarding.
- Users value[integrations](https://www.inventive.ai/integrations) with knowledge sources such as Google Drive, Confluence, Notion, and SharePoint, along with features like conflict detection and source citations.
- Customer support is frequently described as responsive and receptive to product feedback.


Via: Inventive AI


**Limitations**


- G2 reviewers say they'd like **more advanced reporting and analytics** , including better visibility into content usage, adoption, and productivity trends.
- Some users would like **more granular role-based permissions** and workflow controls.
- A few reviewers mention they'd like broader enterprise integrations and additional administrative capabilities.


### **What G2 Reviewers Say About Responsive**


Responsive holds a[4.5/5 rating on G2](https://www.g2.com/products/responsive-formerly-rfpio/reviews) .


**Strengths**


- [G2 reviewers](https://www.g2.com/products/responsive-formerly-rfpio/reviews?qs=pros-and-cons) value Responsive's **content library** , collaboration features, and structured response management workflows.
- Users say the platform helps teams **standardize responses** and collaborate across SMEs more efficiently.
- Reviewers appreciate AI features such as **AI Draft, Smart Search, TRACE Score, and document analysis** for accelerating first drafts and proposal reviews.
- Many users highlight Responsive's integrations and enterprise workflow capabilities.


‍


**Limitations**


- G2 reviewers say the platform has a **steeper learning curve** , particularly because of its features and configuration options.
- Some users describe parts of the interface as **clunky or dated** , requiring more clicks than expected for common tasks.
- Reviewers report that AI-generated responses **sometimes require additional editing** before they're ready for submission.
- Some users would like improvements to formatting, usability, and AI capabilities


Via: Responsive


## **How Inventive AI and Responsive Compare Across Key Capabilities**


Both platforms cover the core proposal workflow, but they differ in where AI is applied, how knowledge is managed, and how much manual work remains for proposal teams.


### **AI Capabilities**


**Inventive AI** is designed from the ground up for AI-powered proposal automation, using AI agents for go/no-go analysis, knowledge retrieval, response generation, proposal review, and AI content governance while keeping humans in control of final approvals.


**Responsive** uses AI on top of its Strategic Response Management platform for document analysis, response generation, proposal review, go/no-go analysis, and[workflow automation.](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/scale-your-rfp-rfi-response-with-automation-and-ai)


### **Knowledge Management**


**Inventive AI** retrieves business knowledge directly from connected systems such as SharePoint, Salesforce, Google Drive, Confluence, Notion, and websites, reducing dependence on a separate Q&A repository. ts[integrations](https://www.inventive.ai/integrations) also cover OneDrive, HubSpot, GitBook, Zendesk, Slack, Teams, and Okta SSO, and SharePoint folder permissions carry over.


**Responsive** combines connected knowledge with a governed Content Library that proposal teams organize, review, and approve over time, giving AI access to both approved responses and connected content.


### **AI Response Quality**


**Inventive AI** analyzes each RFP requirement, retrieves supporting business knowledge, and generates contextual responses with source references. When information is missing, it flags the gap instead of guessing.


**Responsive** generates first drafts using approved Content Library responses, connected knowledge, and prior successful answers. Responses include source citations and a **TRACE Score** that evaluates trustworthiness, relevance, accuracy, and completeness.


### **Narrative Proposal Generation**


**Inventive AI** generates executive summaries, methodologies, implementation plans, statements of work, and other long-form proposal sections while maintaining context across the proposal.


**Responsive** supports long-form proposal creation through reusable content, proposal templates, AI-assisted drafting, and dedicated AI agents such as the Executive Summary Agent.


### **AI Content Governance**


**Inventive AI** has a content governance agent to identify outdated, duplicate, conflicting, and low-quality content before it's reused, reducing manual content maintenance.


[Responsive](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/rfpio-competitors-alternatives) relies on **human-managed content governance** , where content owners review, approve, and maintain reusable responses through approval workflows and governance policies before they're published or reused.


### **Competitive Intelligence**


**Inventive AI** helps proposal teams strengthen competitive positioning by identifying differentiation opportunities and generating competitor-aware proposal content.


**Responsive** supports competitive analysis through customizable AI agents in **Agent Studio** , but does not publicly document out-of-the-box competitor-aware proposal generation.


### **Go/No-Go Decisions**


**Inventive AI** reviews RFP requirements, summarizes key risks, evaluates bid fit against your qualification criteria, and recommends whether an opportunity is worth pursuing.


**Responsive** uses AI-assisted document analysis to summarize RFPs, highlight key requirements, and support go/no-go decisions alongside configurable evaluation workflows.


### **Pricing**


Inventive AI offers simple, usage-based pricing starting at $830/month, billed annually, with unlimited users.


Responsive's price starts at $10,000 a year for its Emerging edition, with named-user licenses; higher-tier plans add advanced AI, automation, and enterprise capabilities.


## **Has AI Changed What Proposal Teams Should Expect from RFP Software?**


AI has changed what proposal teams expect from[RFP software.](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/best-rfp-software)


Earlier platforms helped teams manage content libraries, collaborate with SMEs, route reviews, and reuse approved responses. AI later improved drafting and proposal review, but most of the work still depended on people.


**Today's autonomous agents** handle much more of the proposal process end-to-end. They can understand RFP requirements, retrieve the right business knowledge, generate contextual responses, review proposals for gaps and conflicts, and identify content that needs human approval.


Both platforms reflect this shift. Responsive integrates AI into its Strategic Response Management platform, while Inventive AI is purpose-built to automate proposals end-to-end with AI agents, leaving final review and approval to people.


## **Where Does Human Effort Go in Each Platform?**


Both platforms keep humans involved throughout the proposal process. The difference is where proposal teams spend their time.


With Responsive, proposal teams continue to manage content governance, library maintenance, response approvals, and workflow coordination. AI accelerates drafting, document analysis, proposal review, and qualification, while people remain responsible for keeping library content accurate and up to date.


With Inventive AI, autonomous agents handle much of the repetitive proposal work before review. Instead of managing content and reviewing every response manually, proposal teams can focus on proposal strategy, customer messaging, and final approvals.


For teams managing a high volume of RFPs, the amount of manual work each platform requires becomes an important differentiator.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### Is Responsive or Inventive AI better for enterprise RFP teams?


Both platforms support enterprise proposal teams, but they're designed differently. Responsive is a Strategic Response Management platform with mature workflows, collaboration, and content governance. Inventive AI focuses on automating more of the proposal lifecycle using AI, including response generation, proposal review, and AI content governance, while keeping humans in control of final approvals.


### Can both platforms generate narrative proposals as well as questionnaires?


Yes. Both Inventive AI and Responsive support questionnaires and long-form proposal documents. The difference lies in how responses are generated, reviewed, and maintained throughout the proposal process.


### Do I need a content library to use Inventive AI or Responsive?


Responsive is built around a governed Content Library that proposal teams maintain over time. Inventive AI can retrieve information directly from connected business systems such as SharePoint, Google Drive, Confluence, Salesforce, and Notion, reducing the need to maintain a separate Q&A repository.


### Which platform requires less manual content maintenance?


Responsive relies on content owners to review, approve, and maintain reusable responses. Inventive AI uses AI content governance to identify outdated, duplicate, and conflicting content, helping reduce ongoing maintenance while keeping human reviewers in control of final decisions.


### How should I evaluate AI RFP software during a product demo?


Rather than comparing AI drafting alone, evaluate how each platform retrieves knowledge, handles missing information, supports proposal review, manages content quality, integrates with your existing systems, and scales as your RFP volume grows. Using one of your own active RFPs is often the most reliable way to compare platforms. ‍


### Is Responsive the same as RFPIO?


Yes. RFPIO rebranded as Responsive, and G2 still lists it as Responsive, formerly RFPIO. Should you build an in-house AI RFP tool instead? Most teams shouldn't. Someone has to connect sources, maintain prompts, keep up with model updates, add citations and permissions, and export into each buyer's format. General chat tools also lose context across long RFPs and multi-tab spreadsheets.
